title: ANDS Studio — dossier catalog and new-dossier creation
walkthrough:
You open the dossier catalog. A top bar reads "ANDS Studio" with the subtitle "dossier manager"; on the right are your user chip and links: "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence", and "Guided journey →". Below, the page heading is "Your product dossiers" with a button beside it: "New dossier +". An explanatory paragraph says a Dossier ID "is the permanent file for one product at Health Canada" and that your workspace is isolated from other clients.

If you have no dossiers yet, a notice reads "No dossiers yet. Create one to start building a submission." Otherwise you see a grid of tiles, one per dossier, each showing the dossier ID, product title, a line like "ANDS · CS-BE", a progress bar, and a status chip — either "Ready to file" or a count such as "3/5 modules". Each tile has a "✕" delete button; clicking it pops a browser confirm: "Delete dossier … and all of its documents? This cannot be undone."

Clicking "New dossier +" (the button toggles to "Cancel") reveals a card with two fields: "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"). You must know the ID format — one lowercase letter plus 6–7 digits — or submission fails with the inline error "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". Helper text explains: "Health Canada issues your Dossier ID when you file a Dossier ID Request through REP (via your CESG account)." If you don't have an ID, a small link-style button — "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →" — auto-fills a random d-prefixed draft ID; the text notes "You can set the real ID any time; validation reminds you before filing." Placeholder-ID tiles later carry a chip, "draft ID — set real ✎", which opens a browser prompt asking you to "Enter the Dossier ID issued by Health Canada (one letter + 6–7 digits, e.g. e123456)" and promises "All documents, sequences and history move with it."

You press "Create & open →" (it reads "Creating…" while busy) and are taken straight into the dossier's Module 1 workspace. The top bar now shows the product title and five module tabs, M1–M5, each with a status dot, plus chips for "Application Viewer", "Audit", "Portfolio", and "Journey". The screen is three columns: a section tree on the left, the selected section's panel in the center, and a right rail with a submission tower, module progress ("required sections complete"), and three gate flags: "Documents", "Fee", and "Valid eCTD".
